questions.q: A customer has an ageing TRX-3000 estate. What is IOR's recommended path?
o: Migrate to Yuno II as the direct successor
questions.e: TRX-3000 is legacy with thinning parts availability. Yuno II is the same family with current CPUs, NVMe and Windows 11 IoT — the easy upgrade.

questions.q: What Android version and upgrade path do the lead Urovo models (e.g. RT40S) ship with?
questions.e: RT40S ships on Android 13 with GMS/AER and a stated path to Android 17 — important for 4–5 year deployments.

questions.q: Before pitching Urovo to an enterprise Zebra account, what must the team validate per model?
o: Android LTS/patch cadence and accessory parity (cradles, gun grip, vehicle mount)
questions.e: Enterprise buyers challenge Android version, patch cadence and accessory ecosystem. Validate LTS and accessory parity per model first.

questions.q: What is Datalogic's product focus and IOR's partner status?
o: Data capture — scanners, mobile computers, machine vision, but no printers; IOR is a Datalogic Platinum Partner for UK & Ireland
POS terminals; IOR has no agreement
questions.e: Everything Datalogic makes captures data — fixed retail scanners (#1 globally in bioptic and single-plane), handhelds, mobile computers, industrial scanning and machine vision — and they make no printers. IOR is a Datalogic Platinum Partner for UK & Ireland (signed 2026).

questions.q: Which Epson printer is purpose-built for tablet/cloud POS, with USB-C power delivery and integrated Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in a compact cube?
questions.e: The TM-m30III is the mPOS unit: USB-C PD to power a tablet, integrated Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, tiny footprint, ePOS-Print for cloud apps.

questions.q: Which Aures kiosk lines are built on the same Yuno 27" engine?
questions.e: Komet, Kwartz and Krystal all use the Yuno 27" portrait system, so a customer can standardise terminals and kiosks on one family.

questions.q: Where does Posbank sit in IO Resource's brand mix?
o: IOR's #2 brand overall at ~20% of revenue
questions.e: Posbank is IOR's #2 brand overall at roughly 20% of revenue, and ~35% of the departing rep's book.

questions.q: Across the Apexa range, which best describes the CPU options?
o: From Intel N97/Celeron J6412 up to Core i3 and i5
questions.e: The same Apexa chassis scales from N97/J6412 for light retail up to Core i3/i5 for software-heavy sites.

questions.scenario: A new prospect with no existing scanner fleet asks IOR to recommend a brand for a fresh deployment across their stores.
questions.q: How should the rep position it?
o: Lead with Datalogic as IOR's strategic scanner push, while keeping Honeywell available if the customer specifically wants it
Insist on Honeywell because it's the only good brand
Let the customer pick blind with no recommendation
questions.e: On greenfield deals with no brand preference, Datalogic is IOR's strategic lead. Honeywell remains a fully-supported alternative if requested.
